target.title: RFC 0024: Localization Runtime and Product Coverage
target.body:
## Summary

- defines a small browser/server-safe internal localization kernel plus surface adapters, without replacing existing UI, native-app, or documentation pipelines
- registers OpenClaw's existing 22-locale product union as the v1 baseline, with maturity tracked independently for every locale and surface
- adds representative script, shaping, segmentation, expansion, and bidirectional conformance without falsely advertising test fixtures as supported languages
- defines v1 contracts for runtime messages, Gateway errors, CLI output, localized command/skill metadata, translation review, and release coverage
- projects five owner-coherent implementation PRs, beginning with localization core and ending with completeness gates

## Problem demonstrated

OpenClaw already has substantial localization, but it is surface-specific:

- Control UI ships 21 locales; native localization also includes Swedish
- CLI onboarding supports only English, Simplified Chinese, and Traditional Chinese
- documentation and native apps have independent generated translation workflows
- most CLI output, Gateway errors, channel safety messages, recovery guidance, and capability metadata have no shared locale contract
- Arabic and Persian catalogs exist, but product-wide RTL direction and literal-isolation behavior are not yet a shared guarantee

Representative reports show that these are parts of one cross-owner problem:

| Issue | Demonstrated gap |
| --- | --- |
| openclaw/openclaw#81253 | Exec approval prompts and safety guidance remain hardcoded English |
| openclaw/openclaw#66056 | Gateway/runtime failures lack locale-aware message metadata |
| openclaw/openclaw#88570 | CLI, runtime, channel, and UI coverage remains incomplete |
| openclaw/openclaw#79458 | Slash-command descriptions lack a shared localization model |
| openclaw/openclaw#55239 | Telegram native command-menu descriptions remain English |
| openclaw/openclaw#89971 | Skill names and descriptions remain raw English metadata |
| openclaw/openclaw#28303 | Locale identity and Chinese script/region compatibility need an explicit contract |
| openclaw/openclaw#106576 | Runtime behavior can depend on matching English host error prose |

The full active, historical, duplicate, and landed-foundation mapping is included in the RFC issue catalog.

## Proposed contract

- deterministic BCP 47 locale registry, aliases, inferred-platform matching, fallback chains, and writing direction
- stable product-owned message keys with typed literal parameters, bounded plural/select rules, and reviewed English fallback
- optional Gateway `messageKey` and `messageParams` while preserving existing codes and English `message`
- edge-owned locale resolution for CLI, Control UI, channels, and recipient-specific rendering
- human review for safety, security, authentication, authorization, destructive-action, privacy, and recovery text
- per-surface locale maturity, schema-derived mandatory checks, and per-artifact catalog revisions
- build-time model-assisted translation with provenance; no runtime model dependency for deterministic product messages`n- bundled plugin catalogs under owned namespaces; external localized metadata in v1, with external runtime catalogs deferred until a separately approved Plugin SDK seam

## Five-PR implementation plan

1. Localization core and coverage baseline
2. Runtime safety messages and Gateway errors
3. CLI and TUI localization
4. Localized command, channel, and skill metadata
5. Completeness gates and locale-safe runtime

## Delivery posture

This is foundation-first, not a request to translate the entire repository at once:

- the 22 locales are the existing product registry and coverage baseline, not a simultaneous completeness promise
- PR 1 lands the small internal kernel and connects existing Control UI and wizard consumers without visible behavior changes
- later PRs deepen runtime, CLI/TUI, Gateway, channel, and metadata coverage independently
- each locale/surface pair advances through explicit maturity states; incomplete surfaces retain reviewed English fallback
- external runtime plugin catalogs and generated-content language remain post-v1
- OpenClaw makes no unqualified "fully localized" claim until every required product-owned surface is complete; platform constraints remain disclosed separately

Generated-content language remains a separate post-v1 follow-up because it changes model behavior rather than deterministic product-owned text.

## Owner decisions requested

- Gateway: optional localization metadata on error payloads
- Channels/product: recipient locale ownership and storage
- Command catalog: localized descriptions and channel projections
- Plugin/package: localized metadata fields and host capability/version negotiation
- Release: completeness states and blocking localization gates

## Scope boundary

This RFC does not translate logs, command tokens, config keys, IDs, paths, provider/model names, upstream prose, or arbitrary model-generated responses. English remains the source and compatibility fallback. OpenClaw may claim full product localization only when every required product-owned surface is complete for all 22 baseline locales.

target.title: Plugin-owned external verification approvals
target.body:
## Summary

Adds a draft RFC for plugin-owned external verification of approval resolution. The proposal keeps OpenClaw core as the owner of pending approval state, routing, denial, timeout, cancellation, and final tool continuation, while giving external plugins one narrow route to run verifier-specific proof outside core.

The proposed host surface is intentionally small:

- `requireApproval.externalResolution`: one verifier label, one command template, and allow-style external decisions
- `plugin.approval.resolveVerified`: an ownership-checked resolver for the plugin that created the pending approval

## What changed after review

Updated after maintainer feedback to keep the RFC high-signal:

- rebased on latest `openclaw/rfcs` `main`
- removed PR-history narration from Motivation
- removed safer-auto-mode/blog framing from Motivation and PR notes
- removed durable status-card scope from this RFC
- clarified that auto review does not move approvals into the external-verification lane and requires no change for this boundary
- resolved the previously open decisions in the RFC body:
  - resolver authority uses `operator.approvals`; external plugin helpers must not require `operator.admin`
  - `allow-always` persistence is plugin-owned policy, not a new core auto-approval lane
  - v1 ships command templates only, not arbitrary plugin-defined actions
  - audit fields are approval metadata only; no verifier proof payloads or private IDs in core
  - channels that do not understand `externalResolution` degrade to command text

## Reference implementation

The concrete reference implementation is the AgentKit ClawHub plugin:

- https://github.com/Guardiola31337/openclaw-agentkit
- https://clawhub.ai/plugins/@guardiola31337/agentkit

The RFC now describes AgentKit only in terms of public plugin entry points and the end-user flow, so the host API stays generic and not World-specific.

## Validation

RFC branch validation:

- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`

Reference implementation proof expected before acceptance / implementation:

- `pnpm test:hitl` in `Guardiola31337/openclaw-agentkit`
- `pnpm test:openclaw-hitl` in `Guardiola31337/openclaw-agentkit`
- short manual TUI recording or redacted log showing Verify once, Verify and trust for session, Deny, World QR/link, and resumed protected tool execution

The proof commands and manual user-flow steps are documented in the AgentKit repo; the shareable proof artifact still needs to be attached before this moves out of draft.

target.title: RFC: Claws
target.body:
## Summary

- Defines one Claw package as one complete new OpenClaw agent for one job.
- Makes `claws add` create a new `agents.list[]` entry and workspace; existing agent/workspace collisions fail closed.
- Uses grouped `agent`, `workspace`, `packages`, `mcpServers`, and `cronJobs` ownership boundaries.
- Uses `CLAW.md` YAML frontmatter as the canonical human-authored/exported representation while retaining grouped JSON reads.
- Keeps skills, plugins, MCP servers, heartbeat, and Gateway cron on their existing OpenClaw owner surfaces.
- Uses enclosing `package.json` plus authenticated publishing for package identity, version, and publisher ownership.
- Excludes models, providers, credentials, channel bindings, `agent.skills`, and generic connectors from the portable contract.
- Gates the draft CLI behind `OPENCLAW_EXPERIMENTAL_CLAWS=1`; when disabled, the command is unregistered and absent from help and completions.

## Implementer specifications

- [`CLAW.md` v1](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/blob/f08192f8fd01bec8453249449fe871756f394f2d/rfcs/0016/claw-md-v1-spec.md) defines the YAML 1.2 frontmatter envelope, equivalent JSON form, strict grouped schema, portability constraints, and producer/consumer conformance.
- [Claw Package v1](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/blob/f08192f8fd01bec8453249449fe871756f394f2d/rfcs/0016/claw-package-v1-spec.md) defines package identity/layout, publication validation, exact artifact resolution, owner delegation, provenance, consent, update, and removal semantics.

The RFC remains the product rationale, ownership model, and rollout plan. These sidecars are the concise shared contracts for OpenClaw, ClawHub, and other compatible registry or harness implementations.

## Lifecycle and safety

The lifecycle is `add`, `status`, `update`, `remove`, and `export`. Read-only plans precede consented mutation. Unsupported, blocked, drifted, or ambiguous ownership fails closed.

Grouped update rebuilds its plan immediately before mutation, checks expected workspace presence/content and provenance ownership at the actual mutation boundary, atomically claims package ownership before installers, advances root provenance last, and compensates completed owners in reverse order. Uncertain config/Gateway calls and package installs without artifact rollback are reported as partial rather than cross-owner atomic.

Remove delegates to canonical agent/skill/plugin owners. It uninstalls only a sole, complete, unchanged artifact with artifact-level `claw-installed` origin after its final Claw reference is released and only when no direct install or operator adoption claims it. Pre-existing, independently owned, shared, pending, modified, or ambiguous artifacts are retained and reported.

## Control UI alignment

[openclaw/openclaw#103176](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/103176) remains the Control UI surface for plugin inventory, installation, enablement/disablement, removal, and curated MCP connector discovery. Claws add package references to that shared lifecycle model rather than creating a second package ownership system. A global plugin pinned to another version by a different Claw fails update closed.

Portable MCP declarations remain direct validated `mcp.servers` configuration and do not create a feed-backed connector identity or replace the Control UI's curated connector shelf.

## Implementation stack

The RFC links the ordered twelve-PR OpenClaw stack:

1. [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) grouped schema and add planning
2. [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) agent/root install
3. [#101973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) managed workspace files
4. [#102228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) ClawHub packages and shared uninstall warnings
5. [#102296](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102296) status/remove and owner cleanup
6. [#102306](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102306) export
7. [#102383](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102383) Gateway cron ownership
8. [#102406](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102406) stdio/remote MCP ownership
9. [#102427](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102427) lifecycle diagnostics
10. [#102959](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102959) grouped update planning
11. [#102982](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102982) consented grouped update apply
12. [#106888](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/106888) `CLAW.md` input/export compatibility

The dependent ClawHub track is complete as a four-PR experimental stack:

1. [#3089](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3089) shared Claw schema and storage model
2. [#3090](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3090) publication plus fail-closed reads and public-manifest redaction
3. [#3091](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3091) enabled search, detail, and version APIs with safe summary projection
4. [#3092](https://github.com/openclaw/clawhub/pull/3092) gated hosted feed, safe archive handling, and published-package E2E through real OpenClaw add dry-run

## Validation

- `git diff --check`
- repository-required `Summary` / `Motivation` / `Goals` / `Non-goals` / `Proposal` / `Rationale` / `Unresolved questions` structure
- consistency review against Patrick Erichsen's product, ownership, and removal feedback
- implementation details synchronized with the final repaired OpenClaw and ClawHub stacks
- `CLAW.md` v1 and Claw Package v1 sidecars checked against RFC 0016 and the cumulative implementation branches
- final Codex review: no actionable content issues
